name: Take in client contribution and withdrawal instructions
summary: Clients tell the asset manager when they have cash to invest, such as pension contributions or insurance set-asides, or need cash to pay pensions and benefits. A client reporting analyst logs the instruction, checks signatures and calls the client back on a pre-registered number, then splits the cash across pools and segregated accounts in line with the client's asset mix, which a total portfolio manager approves. Unit subscriptions or redemptions are keyed and released under maker-checker control, and the cash team matches incoming wires or sends outgoing ones with two approvers. Late, changed or very large instructions cause most of the rework and delay, and much of the work is re-keying between email, spreadsheets, the unitholder register and the custodian portal.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Five client portfolios with two to six cash events a month each. Unit dealing and pricing, daily cash management and liquidity forecasting are separate processes; this one ends when the cash has moved and the instruction is closed.

trigger: A client sends a signed notice of cash to invest or cash it needs, with amount, value date and authorisation.
end_state: The instruction is verified, turned into released pool and account instructions, the cash has arrived or been paid to the client's registered account, the client is told, and the log entry is reconciled and closed; or the client cancels.

volume.seasonality: Peaks around month end (pension payroll funding and benefit payments) and year end; occasional large one-off transfers.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file driver. Sources show monthly-scale flows: PSPP contributions and pension payments of about $120 million a month each way in 2021, the insurance client set-asides and monthly payouts with negative net cash flow, and a monthly provincial payment to the judges' plan RCA.

Cost range copied from the organisation file, which uses Job Bank Toronto wages (2023-2024, deflated 9% to 2021) plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading for benefits and overhead; senior investment staff priced from estimated total pay. FTE: logs, verifies, splits and confirms about 16 instructions a month (author estimate).

steps.name: Log the incoming instruction
steps.description: A client reporting analyst picks up the signed instruction from the client service mailbox (a PDF on letterhead or a template sent by the client's treasury), records client, portfolio, contribution or withdrawal, amount, value date and signers in the instruction log, and saves the document.

error.defect_description: Amount or value date keyed wrongly in the log.

evidence.note: No public description of the asset manager's instruction handling; based on common practice at multi-client pooled fund managers.

steps.name: Check signatures and authority
steps.description: The analyst compares the signatures and names with the client's authorised signatory list from account set-up, checks the number of signers the client requires for the amount, and that the account and bank details match those on file.

control.basis: Client authorised signatory list and signing rules set at onboarding (IMA and account set-up)

evidence.note: Author estimate of a 6% discrepancy rate (new signer, missing second signature, changed bank details).

steps.name: Call back the client to confirm
steps.description: A second analyst phones a client contact on the pre-registered call-back list (never a number from the instruction itself), confirms amount, value date and account, and records the name, time and result in the log.

control.basis: Independent call-back on a pre-registered number by a person other than the one who logged the instruction (payment fraud control: verify through a separate channel with contact details already held)

next.condition: client cannot confirm or details differ

evidence.note: Fraud agencies advise verifying payment requests through a separate channel using contact details already held; BEC losses of US$43 billion show the stakes. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Ask the client for a corrected instruction
steps.description: The analyst emails and phones the client's treasury contact explaining the discrepancy and asks for a corrected or re-signed instruction; suspected fraud is escalated to the manager and compliance.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Client sends a corrected or re-signed instruction
steps.description: The client's treasury staff obtain the missing signature, add a new signer to the authorised list or correct the details, and resend the instruction; a few cancel it instead.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check value date, notice and dealing cut-off
steps.description: The analyst checks that the instruction arrived within the agreed notice period and before the pool dealing cut-off for the value date, and flags withdrawals large enough to need the total portfolio team's liquidity view.

error.defect_description: A late instruction is treated as on time, priced at the wrong dealing date.

control.basis: Pool dealing cut-off and client notice periods in the IMA and subscription terms

next.condition: received after cut-off or changed late

evidence.note: Shares are author estimates; the organisation file names late or changed instructions and large same-day withdrawals as the main rework causes.

steps.name: Assess liquidity for a large withdrawal
steps.description: A total portfolio manager checks the client's liquidity report and cash forecast, decides which pools or segregated holdings to draw from without being a forced seller, and whether the amount can be met on the requested date or should be staged.

error.defect_description: Funding source creates an unintended drift from the client's mix.

next.condition: needs a later or staged date

evidence.note: Liquidity managed to avoid forced selling; the insurance client fund has negative net cash flow and monthly liquidity monitoring. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Agree a revised value date with the client
steps.description: The relationship manager calls the client to explain the cut-off or liquidity constraint and agrees a later or staged value date; the client confirms by email or a revised signed instruction.
inputs: timing check result or funding decision

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Draft the split across pools and accounts
steps.description: The analyst applies the client's current flow allocation template, built from its policy targets and the latest drift report, to split the cash between pools (unit subscriptions or redemptions) and segregated accounts or money market holdings.

evidence.note: Flows invested in line with the client's SIP&P and SAA, which the model manager must follow; mechanics are author estimates.

steps.name: Total portfolio manager approves the split
steps.description: A total portfolio manager reviews the split against the client's current weights and pending rebalancing, often using the flow to move the portfolio back toward target instead of trading, and approves or amends it.

control.basis: Client SIP&P targets and ranges, which the IMA requires the manager to follow

evidence.note: The model manager must comply with the client SIP&P including the SAA; 10% amendment rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Enter unit subscription or redemption instructions
steps.description: The analyst keys one instruction per pool into the transfer agency template and unitholder register: client account, pool, subscription or redemption, amount and dealing date, with the call-back evidence attached.

error.defect_description: Wrong pool, amount or dealing date keyed.

evidence.note: Author estimate; a client flow usually becomes two or three pool transactions (organisation file demand drivers).

steps.name: Manager checks and releases the unit instructions
steps.description: The client service manager compares each keyed instruction with the signed client instruction, call-back record and approved split, and releases them to the transfer agency team before the dealing cut-off, or sends them back.

error.defect_description: An error passes the check and is found at unit confirmation.

control.basis: Maker-checker release of unit instructions; units issued only to member accounts on the register (OSC decision of 17 May 2017: pool units distributed only to accredited investor members; accurate books and records)

evidence.note: Conditions on unit distributions and books and records from the OSC decision; review times are author estimates.

steps.name: Notify the cash team and update the cash forecast
steps.description: The analyst emails the cash and collateral team the expected incoming or outgoing amounts, accounts and value dates, and updates the client cash forecast that feeds the weekly liquidity forecast.

error.defect_description: Forecast updated with the wrong date.

evidence.note: Contributions and pension payments were similar in size for the PSPP in 2021 ($1.496 billion and $1.43 billion) while the insurance client fund is net negative, so withdrawals are slightly more frequent; the 55% share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Client wires the contribution
steps.description: On or before the value date the client's treasury wires the cash to its account at the custodian; the analyst waits for the custodian's cash report.

evidence.note: Author estimate: clients give a few business days' notice before the value date.

steps.name: Confirm receipt and match the cash
steps.description: A cash and collateral analyst checks the custodian portal for the incoming wire, matches amount, sender and account to the instruction and confirms to client service that the subscriptions can settle.

error.defect_description: Cash matched to the wrong instruction.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Chase the missing or short contribution
steps.description: The cash analyst contacts the custodian and, through client service, the client's treasury to trace the wire, and tells the transfer agency team so subscriptions are held or adjusted.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for redemption proceeds to settle
steps.description: The pool redemptions are dealt at the next dealing date's unit price and settle to the client's account at the custodian, usually a day or two later.

evidence.note: Daily unit pricing and business-day dealing are assumptions of the organisation file; settlement lag is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the outgoing wire to the client
steps.description: The cash analyst creates a wire in the custodian portal from the client's account to the client's pre-registered bank account for the instructed amount and value date, attaching the instruction and call-back record.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount or value date on the wire.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Second approver releases the wire
steps.description: The cash and collateral manager checks the wire against the instruction and the pre-registered account, confirms it is to the client's own account, and releases it in the custodian portal; wires to new or changed bank details are refused until a fresh call-back is done.

error.defect_description: An error passes the second check.

control.basis: Dual authorisation of outgoing wires and payment only to pre-registered client accounts; changed bank details need separate verification

evidence.note: Verification of account changes through a separate channel advised by fraud agencies; dual approval above thresholds is described in the organisation file's daily cash process. Rates are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm completion to the client
steps.description: The analyst emails the client confirming cash received or paid, the value date and the pool transactions, ahead of the formal unit confirmations from the transfer agency team.
inputs: cash receipt confirmation or released wire

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile and close the instruction
steps.description: At the end of the day the analyst ticks off the instruction against the custodian cash report and the unit confirmations, records any differences for follow-up and closes the log entry.

error.defect_description: A small difference is closed without follow-up.

control.basis: Accurate books and records of member transactions (OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 31(c))

evidence.note: Books and records duty from the OSC decision; mechanics are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Signature or detail discrepancy
exceptions.description: A missing second signer, a new signer not yet on file, changed bank details or a failed call-back sends the instruction back to the client; some are cancelled.

exceptions.name: Large or short-notice withdrawal
exceptions.description: The total portfolio team must decide which pools or holdings to draw from without forced selling, and sometimes asks the client to stage the payment.

exceptions.name: Late or changed instruction
exceptions.description: The instruction arrives after the dealing cut-off or the client changes the amount, so the value date moves after a call with the client.

exceptions.name: Contribution not received
exceptions.description: The client's wire is late, short or sent to the wrong account and must be traced before subscriptions settle.

exceptions.name: Suspected fraudulent instruction
exceptions.description: An instruction with changed bank details fails the call-back; it is escalated to compliance and the client and not processed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt to instruction closed
benchmarks.population: Client cash instructions at a multi-client pooled fund manager

evidence.note: No published benchmark found; set from a few business days' notice before the value date, next-day dealing and one to two days' settlement, with weekends.
About $120 million a month each way.

benchmarks.population: Business email compromise incidents reported worldwide to the FBI

evidence.note: Shows why call-back and dual approval controls are kept.

pain_points.description: Instructions arrive as signed PDFs by email and are re-keyed into a log, a split template, the unitholder register and the custodian portal, with a check at each re-keying.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the systems in the organisation file (register kept with controlled spreadsheets).

pain_points.description: Call-backs depend on reaching a named client contact, which delays same-day processing when contacts are away.

evidence.note: Separate-channel verification is advised; the delay is an author judgement.

pain_points.description: Large or late withdrawals need a liquidity decision and sometimes a staged payment, which the client may not have planned for.

evidence.note: Negative net cash flow at the insurance client and the aim to avoid forced selling.

pain_points.description: Several approvals (portfolio manager, client service manager, cash manager) each wait on a busy person's availability within a fixed dealing cut-off.

evidence.note: Author judgement.

sources.title: 2020/2021 Provincial Judges Pension Board annual report
sources.supports: The model manager engaged March 2020; $421 million transferred and held in money market until a long-term policy is adopted; SIP&P and SAA not finalised by 31 March 2021; province contributing just under $3 million a month to the RCA; member and sponsor contributions flow into the trusts

sources.title: Business Email Compromise: The $43 Billion Scam (Public Service Announcement I-050422-PSA)
sources.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center
sources.supports: US$43.3 billion of exposed losses from 241,206 incidents June 2016 to December 2021, up 65% from July 2019 to December 2021; advises using secondary channels or two-factor authentication to verify requests to change account information

sources.title: Spear phishing (Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre)
sources.supports: Fraudsters spoof trusted senders to request payment changes or urgent wire transfers, often over $100,000; verify unusual requests through a separate channel using contact details already held

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)
sources.supports: IMA with each member under the manager's governing act s. 9(1)2; pool units only to accredited investor members; board-approved policies for KYC, restrictions set out in each IMA built into controls that prevent contraventions, fair allocation of opportunities among members and pools, books and records; PBA fiduciary standard applies to pension clients

sources.title: The model manager (The pension client investments page)
sources.supports: The model manager invests under an investment management agreement and must comply with the pension client's SIP&P including the SAA; regular performance and risk reporting; cost recovery only

sources.title: Our Approach (The model manager web page)
sources.supports: The model manager defines client objectives, risk tolerance and constraints with client boards, actuaries and advisers, runs sensitivity and stress tests including higher inflation, translates the strategic mix into the model manager strategies and keeps liquidity to avoid forced selling

assumptions: No public source describes the asset manager's cash instruction handling; the steps follow common practice at multi-client pooled fund managers and the controls named in the organisation file (call-back lists, two approvers on wires).
Client notice periods of a few business days, next-day dealing and one to two days' settlement are author estimates; they set most of the elapsed time.
Branch shares (6% signature discrepancies, 3% failed call-backs, 12% large withdrawals, 8% late or changed, 55% withdrawals) are author estimates.
The second analyst who does the call-back is shown under the same role id, since the role covers three analysts.
The outgoing wire is modelled here because the organisation file sends a funding wire to daily cash management; incoming cash matching is also shown so the case ends when cash has moved.
Unit confirmations to the client are produced by the pool unit transaction process; this process sends an earlier email confirmation.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges (Job Bank wages, 1.35 loading).
